chunks: And whatever is narrated from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur - may Allah be pleased with them - from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri.

key_terms.السَّنَد: The chain of narrators transmitting a hadith
key_terms.الْمُعَلَّىٰ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْبَصْرِيُّ: Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them, a phrase of approval used for narrators

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-Saduq* in verifying the authenticity of narrations from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri, a key figure in early Shia hadith transmission. By explicitly stating his personal receipt (*samāʿ*) of these reports through multiple chains, including from his father and other trusted scholars, the author reinforces the reliability of the Basri school within the *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. This biographical clarification underscores the importance of continuous, verified chains of transmission (*isnad*) in establishing legal and theological authority in Shia jurisprudence.
